deep.reconstruction:
Context. This sheet is an insertion slip, headed 'Seite 32 unten', for the posthumous text of Riemann's 'Über die Fläche vom kleinsten Inhalt bei gegebener Begrenzung', edited by K. Hattendorff (Abh. Ges. Wiss. Göttingen 13, 1867). The hand appears to be the editor's, but that is a judgement from the image only. The problem is the Plateau problem for a minimal surface bounded by nu straight lines. The surface is parametrised over a half-plane in t, where real t corresponds to the boundary. Earlier quantities, not on this page, are du, dv (with v linked to u by eq. (17)), the Gauss-map variable H (written eta elsewhere: the stereographic image of the normal), and a second-order linear ODE
  d^2k/dv^2 = Q k,  with Q = (1/k) d^2k/dv^2.
Q is built from a rational function F(t), of which 2nu-7 coefficients are still free (accessory parameters).

Step 1 (claim). The remaining 2nu-7 coefficients of F(t) must be real. This is reduced to showing that Q = (1/k) k'' is real for real t.

Step 2 (boundary behaviour of du and dv). On p. 12 it was shown that du is real or purely imaginary along every straight boundary line. Hence the same holds at every boundary point of the mapped regions (the t-half-plane). By eq. (17) the same holds for dv.

Step 3 (local normal form of the Gauss map on one boundary arc). Along a straight boundary segment the surface normal is perpendicular to the line. So the image of that segment on the unit sphere lies on a great circle.
- Riemann takes the tangent plane at the pole of that great circle as the plane of a new variable eta_1.
- He rotates the sphere by a Moebius map eta_1 = e^{i theta_1} (alpha_1 - H)/(1 + alpha_1' H).
- Here alpha_1' should be the complex conjugate of alpha_1; that is Riemann's priming convention and is what makes the map a rotation.
- Under this map the great-circle arc goes to a circle |eta_1| = const centred at 0. So on that boundary piece eta_1 = c e^{i phi} with phi real.

Step 4 (solutions of the ODE in terms of eta_1). The page ends with k_1' = sqrt(dv/d eta_1) and k_2' = eta_1 sqrt(dv/d eta_1), called the particular integrals. Completion (mine, standard):
- If eta_1 = k_2/k_1 is a ratio of solutions of k'' = Q k with Wronskian k_1 k_2' - k_2 k_1' = 1, then d eta_1/dv = 1/k_1^2.
- Hence k_1 = (dv/d eta_1)^{1/2} and k_2 = eta_1 k_1, and Q = k_i''/k_i = -(1/2){eta_1, v}, the Schwarzian derivative.
- The Schwarzian is invariant under the Moebius change from H to eta_1, so Q is the same whichever boundary arc is used.

Step 5 (the reality proof, presumably continued on the next sheet). On the arc, with eta_1 = c e^{i phi}, one has {eta_1, v} = {phi, v} + (1/2)(d phi/dv)^2.
- If dv is real, phi is a real function of real v, so this is real.
- If dv is imaginary, put v = i s. Then (d phi/dv)^2 = -(d phi/ds)^2 and {phi, v} = -{phi, s}, so it is again real.
- Hence Q is real on the whole real t-axis.
- By the reflection principle, F then has real coefficients.
errors: The constant alpha_1' must be the complex conjugate of alpha_1, otherwise the Moebius map is not a rotation of the sphere. This matches Riemann's convention of priming conjugates but is not stated on the page.
Projecting onto the tangent plane at the pole (from the antipode) sends the great circle to |eta_1| = 2, not 1. Only constancy of |eta_1| matters, so this is harmless.
The asterisk in 'theta_1^*' (among the constants) does not match 'theta_1' in the formula. It is probably a stray mark or a transcription artefact, not a mathematical slip.
The count 2nu-7 of free coefficients cannot be checked from this page alone, since F(t) is defined on the referenced page 32.

results.what: Gauss image of a straight boundary line of a minimal surface lies on a great circle; rotate it to |eta_1| = const by a unitary Moebius map
results.modern_name: Gauss map / Schwarz reflection for minimal surfaces with straight boundary

results.what: sqrt(dv/d eta) and eta*sqrt(dv/d eta) as two solutions of k'' = Q k, with Q = (1/k) k'' equal to -1/2 times the Schwarzian of eta in v
results.modern_name: Schwarzian derivative / linearisation of the Schwarzian equation by a 2nd-order Fuchsian ODE

results.what: Reality of Q on the real t-axis, hence real accessory parameters (2nu-7 real constants)
results.modern_name: reality of accessory parameters for Fuchsian equations of polygonal (circular-arc) maps
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann/Hattendorff 1867; Schwarz; Darboux; Garnier for the Plateau problem

deep.surprise_reason: This is an editorial insertion belonging to Riemann's posthumously published minimal-surface memoir (Hattendorff 1867). The Schwarzian/Fuchsian-equation approach to polygonal Plateau problems is already attributed to Riemann there; the page only supplies a detail of a published argument.

checkable.sympy: v=symbols('v'); e=Function('eta')(v); k1=1/sqrt(diff(e,v)); k2=e/sqrt(diff(e,v)); simplify(diff(k2,v,2)/k2 - diff(k1,v,2)/k1)
checkable.asserts: k1 and k2 satisfy the same equation k''=Qk, i.e. the result is 0
Schwarzian is Moebius invariant, so Q is the same in H and eta_1 (result 0)
{e^{i phi}, v} = {phi,v} + phi'^2/2, which is real for real phi and real v (result 0)

transcription_corrections: 'Zu folge dieses größten Kreises' should read 'Im Pole dieses größten Kreises legen wir die Tangential-Ebene an', i.e. the tangent plane at the pole of the great circle.
'theta_1^*' in the list of constants is probably just theta_1 (or theta_1'); the asterisk looks like a stray mark.
'W.' in the margin is an editorial mark, not part of the text.
